title: San Francisco 49ers and Las Vegas Raiders fans ejected, arrested after violent fights at Levi's Stadium: Santa Clara police
text:
San Francisco 49ers and Las Vegas Raiders fans ejected, arrested after violent fights at Levi's Stadium: Santa Clara police - ABC7 San Francisco 
 24/7 Live San Francisco East Bay South Bay Peninsula North Bay SPORTS 
 49ers and Raiders fans ejected, arrested after fights at Levi's Stadium: 'We gotta be better' 
 GRAPHIC CONTENT WARNING: Some of these videos may be disturbing to watch. 
 Santa Clara police made arrests and ejections after violent fights broke out at Sunday's game between the 49ers and the Raiders at Levi's Stadium. Frisco Philly/Storyful By J.R. Stone Wednesday, November 11, 2026 5:48AM Share Follow ABC7 on Google SANTA CLARA, Calif. (KGO) -- Santa Clara police arrested 11 people and ejected 45 others after multiple violent fights broke out during and after Sunday's game between the San Francisco 49ers and the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi's Stadium.
 On Thursday, police arrested a 32-year-old San Jose resident who is suspected in the violent beating.
 Videos circulating on social media showed altercations in the stands, concourse areas and parking lots. Two videos provided to ABC7 showed punches being thrown and a large fight inside the stadium.
 One of those videos was recorded by 49ers fan Ken Winland.
 "And next thing you know, they were in a full-on brawl," Winland said. "It was just a straight-on attack. And then, as you can see, people came up the aisle and came out of nowhere and didn't see that coming. It turned into, at one point a 4 or 5-person brawl, and people and bodies were going left and right."
 Around a dozen fight videos have surfaced online from the rivalry game between the 49ers and Raiders.
 MORE: 49ers capitalize on 5 2nd-half takeaways to cruise past Raiders 38-17 
 One of the most serious incidents appeared to occur in the parking lot outside Levi's Stadium, where video showed two people being punched and knocked unconscious.
 "But you could just feel that this was, you know, the 'Battle of the Bay' rivalry, even though they're in Las Vegas now," said 49ers fan Steven Gomez.
 Police said they had no update on the condition of the people seen lying on the ground after being struck.
 Gomez said he did not witness the parking lot fight but recorded a separate altercation from his seat inside the stadium.
 "The thing that kind of gave me the like, 'Oh my god, I saw a woman get struck in her face!'" Gomez said.
 A Raiders fan who spoke Monday evening shared photos of a vehicle with a broken window. She said at least four other vehicles parked in an off-site lot also had windows shattered after the game.

 "It's always fun to banter with Raiders fans and stuff, but we gotta be better. I want to take my youngest son to a game and as far as Niners/Raiders, like I just don't think I can do that. It just leads you with your child like too vulnerable," Gomez said.
 In a statement, Santa Clara police said fan violence at large-scale events will not be tolerated and that officers and security personnel responded to all known incidents during and after Sunday's game.
 "The Santa Clara Police Department is aware of several incidents of fan-on-fan violence that occurred during and after Sunday's game at Levi's Stadium," the department said. "On Sunday, there were numerous arrests (11) and ejections (45) that occurred during the event."
 Police said several incidents remain under investigation and noted that some fights involved victims who were unwilling to cooperate with investigators.
 The department said it sought assistance from approximately 30 outside law enforcement agencies for the event and plans to pursue those responsible for acts of violence.
 "We will seek to arrest the individuals responsible for the fan-on-fan violence at the event," the department said.
 The 49ers also issued a statement, saying: "We have a zero-tolerance policy for violence at Levi's Stadium. The Santa Clara Police Department, our security and guest services teams responded to several incidents throughout Sunday's game. We are grateful to all personnel for their swift response and dedication to maintaining a safe environment for all fans."
 Police are asking anyone who witnessed the incidents or recorded video to contact the Santa Clara Police Department.
